Project Title: Integrating Mobility Data, Survey Responses, and Forecasting Information to Enhance Understanding of Decision-Making During Hazardous Weather Events in Communities
Project Goal: The primary goal of the proposed project is to integrate cell-phone mobility data and survey responses to develop a comprehensive understanding of population mobility in response to hazardous weather information.
Research Keywords: Decision Support, Risk Perception & Response, Social Vulnerability, "Social, Behavioral, and Economic Sciences (SBES)"
Project Description: A database of hazardous weather information (warning and evacuation orders) for hurricanes, wildfires, and flash floods will be created to study its effects on mobility responses. Econometric methods for casual interference and cell-phone mobility data will be used to analyze how diverse socioeconomic groups react to hazardous weather information for both short- and long-fused weather events. Surveys will be integrated with mobility data to address biases in existing evacuation analyses, to enhance understanding of mobility responses from underserved populations, and to estimate variations in evacuation costs and the impact of forecast accuracy on decision-making.
Project Benefits: This project will enhance preparedness and responses to hazardous weather, particularly for underserved communities by providing research-based recommendations to improve evaluation tools, the understanding of socioeconomic disparities in hazardous weather event responses, and the forecast accuracy impacts. The creation of a comprehensive dataset will provide resources for refining warning systems and decision-making.

Project Title: Precipitation Prediction Grand Challenge: Using Quick Response Surveys to Develop and Pilot Test Flood Risk Communications
Project Goal: Using the WPO-funded Quick Response Survey (QRS) database on individual response to hazards, this project will research and validate plain-language flood risk (including flash floods) communication guidance for potential adoption by the National Weather Service forecasters and Integrated Warning Team partners.
Research Keywords: Precipitation Grand Challenge, Community Preparedness & Resilience, Decision-Making, Risk Communication, Risk Perception & Response, "Social, Behavioral, and Economic Sciences (SBES)"
Project Description: Using QRS data, this project will evaluate how flood risk exposure differs between people who were unaware of flood risk and those who were aware and prepared in advance. These insights will be used to iteratively develop and pilot test risk communication concepts through focus groups, surveys, and input from the National Weather Service, emergency managers, and media partners. The outcome will be a prototype library of plain-language flood messages for forecasters to deploy as selectable components with in AWIPS or others.
Project Benefits: This project will demonstrate how behavioral research can be translated into operationally useful products that support improved outcomes for the public. It provides and empirically grounded approach to developing flood messages that aligns with how people actually experience risk and make decisions during flood events.
